I farm the same 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize cycle, so I will put all 10.1 mu into wheat first, then all 10.1 mu into summer maize after wheat harvest. I do not like changing too much if last year was acceptable. I start from what I already know works here, then I adjust a little by price and by what the better fields around me are doing. Fertilizer costs real money, but losing grain costs more, so I will not cut fertilizer too hard. With well water in hand, I will make sure the crop does not get stuck when it needs water. For wheat, I will use an improved variety because that is what many people around me plant now and I have seen it yield better than old seed. I will put enough base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress nitrogen around jointing. Wheat needs more water on my land, so I will irrigate about 3 times if the season is normal. After wheat harvest, I will seed summer maize quickly. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is already the common way here and it gives fuller ears if fertilizer and water keep up. I will keep maize management simple: one main fertilizer plan, two irrigations if rain is not enough, and spray when weeds or insects show up. On tillage, I will rotary till for wheat because I have time after maize, but for summer maize I will do no-tillage seeding right after wheat harvest to save time and catch moisture. I am aiming for a steady harvest, not gambling on cutting inputs too much.
